classification.difficultyReason: Identify two quadrants and two square-minus-quadrant regions whose circular areas cancel.

content.prompt: The figure below is constructed from four identical arcs, and each is one quarter of the circumference of a circle of radius $r$. Find the area of the figure.

spec.description: Four quarter-circle arcs join the top, left, bottom and right scaffold endpoints. Upper-left and lower-right boundaries bulge outward; the other two are inward arcs. Both complete perpendicular dashed scaffold segments are retained.
spec.mathematics: Each half-scaffold has length r. Upper-left and lower-right regions are radius-r quadrants; the other two regions are radius-r squares with one quadrant removed.
spec.answerVisibility: No radius labels or solution divisions are added.

answer.short:
$2r^2$

Pair each quadrant with a square-minus-quadrant region.
answer.worked:
The dashed lines divide the figure into two quarter circles of radius $r$ and two $r$-by-$r$ squares with a quarter circle removed.

$$\begin{align*}A&=2\left(\frac{\pi r^2}{4}\right)+2\left(r^2-\frac{\pi r^2}{4}\right)\\A&=\frac{\pi r^2}{2}+2r^2-\frac{\pi r^2}{2}\\A&=2r^2.\end{align*}$$
